quotes.text: T-SQL is where you make meaning enforceable. With explicit schema constraints and validation gates, you can force the warehouse boundary to behave like a boundary.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes T-SQL from a query tool into the contract layer of a data platform.

quotes.text: Your query text is not the truth. The plan is the truth. The text is your request. The plan is the platform's interpretation of your request under cost constraints, statistics, and available indexes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why execution plans, not query text, determine cost and behavior.

quotes.text: A stable plan is predictable compute. An unstable plan is conditional chaos with a credit card attached.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Ties plan stability directly to cloud cost predictability.

quotes.text: Fabric makes it easy to move data. It does not make it safe to move meaning.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the core risk of convenience tooling in modern data platforms.

quotes.text: So the rule for AI in enterprise data systems is simple. AI can draft queries. Humans must enforce contracts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear rule for using AI-generated SQL safely.

chapters.title: AI-written SQL and the operating model

takeaways: Treat the Fabric warehouse as an enforced boundary with explicit schemas, constraints and validation gates instead of fixing bad data downstream in Power BI.
Use execution plans as acceptance criteria and manage parameter sniffing, statistics, indexing and partitioning to keep cost and performance predictable.
Encode least privilege and business logic in schemas, roles, views and stored procedures, and let AI draft queries only while humans enforce shape, access and cost.
hook: Microsoft Fabric did not make SQL optional; it moved T-SQL to where cost overruns, audit findings and performance incidents begin. This episode is for data engineers and platform architects running modern Microsoft data platforms. It shows how to use T-SQL to enforce shape, access and cost so the platform stays deterministic instead of drifting into entropy.
